summary: Checked this year's YouTube policy changes for How Tech Works and added 3 Shorts topics from references rising now (tunnel boring machine, the Paris Metro's rubber tyres, AI-generated GPU frames).
why: Owner note of 19 Nov (topics gaining traction): each new topic's reference adds 113K-542K views a day. The Partner Program bar doubles on 1 Feb 2027, which makes the weekly long video this channel's realistic route to monetisation.

findings.title: Monetisation bar doubles on 1 Feb 2027
findings.detail: New applicants need 8,000 watch hours (now 4,000) or 20M Shorts views in 90 days (now 10M); Shorts pay needs 10M qualified views every 90 days. For this channel: the long videos are the route (about 40,000 full views of a 12-minute video).

findings.title: AI labels don't apply to our animated videos
findings.detail: Disclosure covers photorealistic AI; YouTube self-labels it since 27 May 2026. Ours are clearly illustrations.

findings.title: Inauthentic content targets template channels
findings.detail: Mass-produced, repetitive videos lose monetisation channel-wide; our variety rules and directed pictures are the defence.

findings.title: Trains and machines still lead the niche
findings.detail: Rubber-tyred train Short 542K views a day, Logibu's boring machine 245K a day on a 36K channel.

changes.title: 3 topics added to the feed
changes.detail: tbm-under-london (9.28), paris-metro-tyres (8.93), gpu-invents-frames (8.05); all global, core formats, 5 sourced facts each.
